In late 2023, two Nature papers made a strong impression: Google DeepMind announced 2.2 million predicted crystals, 380,000 of them stable, and Berkeley’s robotic laboratory A-Lab said it had synthesised 41 new compounds in 17 days. Three years on, this work remains a milestone, but also a textbook case of controversy: solid-state chemists dispute the novelty of many of the materials and the quality of the automated analyses. In the meantime, “autonomous laboratories” have multiplied, funded by start-ups, states and cloud giants. What is a materials prediction worth until the material has been made, characterised and used?
En science des matériaux, le chemin entr: In materials science, the path from an idea to a product involves at least four steps: predicting that a compound is stable, synthesising it, verifying that this compound has indeed been obtained, then demonstrating that it has a useful property, at industrial scale. AI has massively accelerated the first step. The question is whether it also accelerates the next three, and at what cost to rigour.

Periodic Labs, start-up américaine, résu: Periodic Labs, a US start-up, neatly sums up the loop it is aiming for: formulating a target from stability and property predictions, predicting how to synthesise it, then determining what has actually been made and whether it has the desired properties (Periodic Labs). The third step, characterisation, is the most neglected in announcements and the most criticised by specialists.
Selon <a href=\"https://deepmind.google/: According to Google DeepMind (29 November 2023), GNoME, a graph neural network trained on Materials Project data, proposed 2.2 million new crystals, 380,000 of which lie on the final convex hull, after DFT verification. The company states that 736 of these structures have been made experimentally by outside teams. Level: P for the prediction method (Nature), BI for the interpretation (“800 years of knowledge”).
Critique : Anthony Cheetham et Ram Sesha: Criticism: Anthony Cheetham and Ram Seshadri (UC Santa Barbara) examined a random sample of these structures in Chemistry of Materials (2024) and cast doubt on the novelty and usefulness of many entries (404 Media). The debate is less about the calculations than about what should be called a “new material”.
A-Lab : la synthèse robotisée et sa cont: A-Lab: robotic synthesis and the challenge to it
L&#39;article de <a href=\"https://www.n: The Nature paper (November 2023) reports that the A-Lab at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory obtained 41 of 58 targets in 17 days and 355 experiments. Details often omitted: 35 of the 41 successes used literature-inspired recipes; only 37% of the 355 recipes produced their target; slow kinetics explains 11 of the 17 failures, and the algorithm could neither regrind nor heat for longer.
En mars 2024, Josh Leeman, Leslie Schoop: In March 2024, Josh Leeman, Leslie Schoop (Princeton), Robert Palgrave (University College London) and their colleagues published a reanalysis in PRX Energy. According to Chemistry World, they fault the system for ignoring compositional disorder: in Palgrave’s words, “two-thirds of their predictions were simply ordered versions of compounds already known to be disordered”. They also criticise the automated Rietveld refinement. Palgrave’s conclusion: “it is likely that they made no discoveries”. Gerbrand Ceder, who led the project, responded by publishing additional data that he considers confirm the syntheses. Susan Latturner (Florida State University) believes that “a competent human” is still needed to determine what has actually been made.
Ce débat ne disqualifie pas l&#39;automa: This debate does not discredit the automation of synthesis, which works. It shows that the interpretation step, entrusted to AI, was the weak link.
Microsoft Research a publié MatterGen da: Microsoft Research published MatterGen in Nature in January 2025 (doi 10.1038/s41586-025-08628-5): a generative model that proposes inorganic structures according to targeted properties (composition, symmetry, mechanical or magnetic properties). The paper includes a proof-of-concept experimental synthesis; this is a single example, not a statistical validation.
Neon, modèle d&#39;un trillion de paramè: Neon, a trillion-parameter model post-trained to analyse XRD, deployed in laboratories running 24 hours a day; targets: superconductors, magnets
Microsoft Discovery, plateforme unifiant: Microsoft Discovery, a platform unifying models, simulation and experiments, now available; direct connection to PNNL’s laboratory automation; $60 million ($40 million in Azure credits, $20 million in services)
Standard de connexion entre modèles et i: Connection standard between models and instruments; at Carnegie Mellon, drivers and orchestration written in about 8 hours, six deliberately induced hazardous situations blocked before any movement, experiments about three times faster

Un exemple instructif du standard d&#39;: An instructive example of Anthropic’s standard: at Carnegie Mellon, the agent rejected a saturated measurement on its own initiative (R² coefficient below 0.9), reran the experiment at half the concentration and accepted a fit with R² above 0.98 (Anthropic). This is exactly the quality-control task that the A-Lab lacked in 2023. But it is a demonstration chosen by the company.
Le reportage de Nature « Inside the self: Nature’s feature “Inside the self-driving lab revolution” (April 2026) takes stock of this movement and its implications for careers (Nature/PubMed).
Les applications énergétiques sont l&#39: Energy applications are the main argument for funding: batteries, ionic conductors, catalysts, materials for fusion. GNoME claims 528 potential lithium-ion conductors (Google DeepMind); Microsoft says it cuts the analysis of data on energy-storage materials “from years to weeks” (Microsoft). These figures are predictions or claims: none of the sources consulted documents an AI-discovered material deployed industrially in a commercial battery (information not confirmed).

La nouveauté : un composé substitué ou d: Novelty: is a substituted or doped compound a “new material”? The community has no shared convention.
La synthétisabilité : stable selon la DF: Synthesisability: stable according to DFT does not mean manufacturable under realistic conditions.
Les données négatives : les échecs de sy: Negative data: synthesis failures are rarely published, which biases model training. Autonomous laboratories produce these failures systematically; it remains to be seen whether they will be shared or kept as a competitive advantage.
La reproductibilité : les systèmes privé: Reproducibility: private systems (Periodic Labs, Microsoft Discovery) publish neither their data nor complete protocols.
Le passage à l&#39;échelle : entre quelq: Scale-up: between a few grams and industrial production, the obstacles are mainly ones of process, not of prediction.

Les montants restent modestes face à ceu: The sums remain modest compared with those for language models, but the logic is strategic: magnets without rare earths, batteries without critical metals, catalysts for hydrogen. In the United States, Periodic Labs and Radical AI are among the 24 organisations that have signed agreements with the Department of Energy for the Genesis Mission (DOE). In the United Kingdom, the AI for Science strategy provides for a call to develop autonomous laboratory platforms and cites Liverpool’s Materials Innovation Factory (techUK). In China, the Beijing municipal government published a plan in July 2026 aiming for autonomous laboratories combining AI, robotics and high-throughput instruments by 2028; single-source information (state media outlet ECNS), details not confirmed (Let's Data Science).
En France, l&#39;outil principal est le: In France, the main vehicle is the exploratory PEPR DIADEM, co-led by the CNRS and the CEA, with funding of around €85 million over eight years since 2022, which structures four platforms for synthesis, high-throughput characterisation, simulation and AI-based data exploitation (CNRS). It draws on the large-scale facilities SOLEIL and ESRF. The CNRS has set the goal of cutting the identification cycle for a material from 20 years to 4 to 10 years (CNRS, list of PEPRs): this is a goal, not a result. We found no public source documenting a closed-loop autonomous laboratory on the scale of A-Lab in France (information not confirmed).
Deux atouts européens méritent d&#39;êtr: Two European assets deserve emphasis: the density of large-scale facilities (synchrotrons, neutron sources), which provide high-quality characterisation data, and a solid-state chemistry culture that has produced precisely the most robust criticisms. The main risk is that the data from these public infrastructures will mainly serve to train foreign private models.
Dernier enjeu, la sécurité : la chimie p: A final issue is security: chemistry shares a dual-use risk with biology (toxic molecules, explosives). Anthropic’s standard incorporates hardware interlocks, which is a step in the right direction, but no public standard yet governs the connection of AI agents to laboratory instruments.

L&#39;IA a résolu le problème de l&#39;a: AI has solved the problem of producing candidates in abundance and is starting to automate synthesis. The bottleneck has shifted to characterisation and interpretation: knowing what has really been made. This is where the A-Lab controversy is valuable, and this is where human expertise, large public facilities and the sharing of negative data remain decisive. For Europe, the comparative advantage lies less in the model than in the instrument and high-quality data.
